title: Tests, CI and the build
grade_reasons: C stands, at the low end of the band. The base is sound (325,579 lines of tests with no snapshots, a test database built once, a docs-only push that runs nothing, a gate before each deploy), but one push type-checks the same commit five times and builds it three times in CI, the gate takes 5 min 11 s where 90 s would do, and about 27 runner-minutes of every push are repeats. It is not a B because not one number is held while the production build runs at 90% of its machine and was killed once on 11 November; it is not a D because the integration and browser suites, most of a push's runner time, run close to what they need, and nobody is hurt.
verdict_on_bar: KEPT, after checking each floor. One lint, one schema check and one check of the whole program per push, and 2 builds in CI. Once is the floor, and I checked that the hosts build cannot be shared: with the store domain set, every /s/ address redirects to the store's own host (src/lib/store-hosts.ts:89), so the main suite cannot run on that build. The unit run at 3 min 30 s: I redid the sum from the file counts (934, 214 and 67, counted again) and it is what step 0.39 reaches with 7 s to spare. A stricter figure would rest on trials that may show a fresh worker is needed, and the bar already makes the ceiling follow them. 8 minutes for the slowest job a release waits for, and 3 shards a suite. The type check at 60 s: Next 16.4 runs the project's own tsc and its docs cover TypeScript 7 (node_modules/next/dist/docs, the typescript config page), whose native compiler should check the whole program well inside that. I could not time it (a type check was ruled out for the panel), so the line stays at 60 s and the ratchet takes it lower. TIGHTENED. (1) The gate: 90 s, not 120. The steward's own three lines (15, 60 and 15 s) add up to 90 and nothing explained the other 30. (2) The build's memory: 75% of the machine stays as the outer line, and a ceiling at the median of ten builds plus 10% is added. On a 16 GB machine this review's build sits at 46%, so a 75% line alone lets the build grow by more than half unseen, and it used up 0.8 GB of room between 28 October and 11 November. (3) The pre-push rule: the bar now covers a session's first push. A cloud session starts with no lint cache and no build info and many push once, so a tolerance for 'the first' exempted the common case. (4) One type check means one. The gate may check the app without tests only while the whole program takes over 60 s, so step 2.42 should try the native compiler before it makes a second tsconfig. (5) Seconds with a 25% band do not hold this area. Three of phase 0's gains are smaller than the band: the schema back in the database client is 6% of a shard, Drizzle unbundled 9%, the test database built again for the gate 7%. So the configuration that makes each gain is held exactly, the setup share is read from Vitest's own line, and a weekly check keeps every ceiling near its median. (6) The slowest job is a median that must be reached, with 10 minutes for a single run. In step 1.20 it is only a ceiling written into a file. CORRECTED. The 4 GB line for the type check stays, for a session's memory. Its stated reason goes: 4 GB on top of a 5.8 GB compile does not fit an 8 GB build machine, and a check inside the production build would be a second check of a commit the gate has passed. A cold lint after a lockfile change is recorded under its own label, not held to 15 s. The import cycle leaves this area's count: it is the server's measure and step 1.8 holds it. ADDED. The time from push to live, recorded and held. It is what the owner waits for and nothing records it. No honest number exists before the first ten readings, so the bar is its parts (a 90 s gate, a held build) and a ceiling that only falls. Runner-minutes per push and install seconds, printed. And a count that all 1,215 unit test files still run after the split into projects. NOT MEASURABLE AS WRITTEN. scripts/timed.mjs and scripts/ci-budgets.json do not exist; step 1.20 makes them. 'The median of the last ten runs' had nothing that reads ten runs, and the per-file figures were samples timed by hand. The first proposed addition covers both.

measures.name: How often one commit is checked, built and deployed on a push
measures.today: 5 full type checks (static, the gate, and inside the e2e, hosts and signed-in builds), 2 lints, 3 schema checks, 3 builds in CI and a fourth on Vercel, 8 installs on 9 runners (re-read in .github/workflows/ci.yml: lines 55-56, 110, 152, 206, 249, 299-302). 6 of the last 75 commits that ran CI changed only tests and still deployed. About 27 runner-minutes of a push are repeats by the findings' figures: 12 of type checks (183 s each, measured), about 6 of lint, 3.6 of imports in the integration files, 2.2 of unit setup and about 3.5 for the third build (samples and estimates).
measures.target_a: 1 lint, 1 schema check and 1 type check of the whole program per push. 2 builds in CI: one for the browser suites, one for the hosts job. 0 deploys for a push that cannot change the deployed app. While the whole program takes more than 60 s to check, and only then, the gate may check the app without tests and the static job the whole.
measures.how_measured: src/lib/ci-once.scan.test.ts, which step 0.38 makes beside src/lib/ci-playwright.scan.test.ts and step 3.18 lowers: it reads ci.yml, counts the jobs that run pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm db:check and pnpm build on a push, and fails above the counts or when a job that builds lacks SKIP_BUILD_TYPECHECK. Skipped deploys are read from the pending job's log.

measures.name: The deploy gate, and the time from push to live
measures.today: 5 min 11 s for lint, the type check and six test files on CI run 1160 (code review step 0.2). Lint re-reads 6,213 files with no cache. The type check is one program of 8,003 files: 183 s in this machine's build, under a 7,168 MB heap limit. The time from push to live is recorded nowhere: scripts/await-deploy.mjs knows the moment and prints no duration, and Vercel's build prints no seconds.
measures.target_a: The gate's three steps: a median of 90 s or less. Lint 15 s with its cache restored, the type check 60 s within 4 GB of memory, the money tests 15 s. If the owner puts a test run in the gate (step 2.43), its seconds are added to the line and held with it: about 60 to 100 s for a related run, 3 min 30 s for the whole suite. Push to live: recorded on every deploy and held by a ceiling that only falls; the first ten readings set it.
measures.how_measured: scripts/timed.mjs and scripts/ci-budgets.json (step 1.20 makes both): each step's seconds in the run's summary and a failed run above a ceiling, read as the median of ten runs. scripts/await-deploy.mjs writes the seconds from the push to production reporting the commit (step 1.20).

measures.name: The unit run (pnpm test)
measures.today: 5 min 34 s for 1,215 files in an agent sandbox (code review step 0.4, 10 November). A plain unit file costs 0.48 s, 0.34 s of it the admin's English and a fresh worker it cannot use. Setup is 40 to 41% of the run on a 187-file sample. Component files cost 0.74 s each (22 sampled), database files 3.0 s (8 sampled). Counted again here: 934 plain, 214 component and 67 database files.
measures.target_a: 3 min 30 s or less on a machine where it takes 5 min 34 s today, and CI's median held. Setup under 10% of Vitest's duration line. A plain unit file at 0.15 s or less. All 1,215 files still run, each in exactly one project. For the 281 component and database files: a lower figure per file, or a recorded trial that shows the fresh worker is needed. The ceiling follows the trials: about 3 minutes if the component trial passes.
measures.how_measured: Vitest's own duration line, which splits setup, import and tests, read by scripts/timed.mjs (step 1.20). The proposed addition makes it fail above 10% setup and compare files run with files on disk, and makes a scan test hold the three projects. Per-file figures by running the 187-, 22- and 8-file samples again at steps 0.39, 2.44 and 4.5.

measures.name: The jobs a migration release waits for
measures.today: Not recorded. The workflow's own comment says about 10 minutes side by side (ci.yml:40); the timeouts are 20 to 30 minutes. 556 integration files run one at a time in 3 shards, and 525 of them spend 0.48 s importing the database client: about 85 s a shard. Each browser job's build type-checks for about 3 minutes. Playwright sets no workers and no shards for 573 and 208 tests, and a test that passes on its one retry is counted nowhere. 18 of 75 recent commits carried a migration and waited for every job.
measures.target_a: The median of every job a release waits for: 8 minutes or less, and no single run over 10. At most 3 shards a suite. The database client's import at 0.10 s a file or less (0.07 s measured with the schema gone and Drizzle pre-bundled). Tests that pass only on a retry: counted on every run and held at the median plus 2.
measures.how_measured: scripts/timed.mjs around each shard, each Playwright run and each build, with ceilings in scripts/ci-budgets.json (step 1.20). Retried tests from Playwright's JSON report (step 1.20). The client's import by the 20-file probe at step 0.39 and again at 4.5; its two causes (no schema in src/db/client.ts, Drizzle pre-bundled) by the proposed scan.

measures.name: The production build: peak memory against its machine
measures.today: About 7.2 GB of 8 on Vercel (90%), with the type check, the build cache and two of three workers already off. It had 0.8 GB of room on 28 October and was killed for memory once on 11 November (docs/build-memory.md:18, 40-46). On this review's 16 GB machine, with all three on: 263 s and 7.61 GB for the whole machine, 46% (m/build-summary.txt). No build prints either figure: scripts/next-build.mjs is ten lines and measures nothing. The page worker runs with source maps on, 4.7 MB of heap per MB of server code (AS-10), never measured in a whole build.
measures.target_a: Every production build prints its seconds and its peak. The peak is 75% of its machine or less, and its ceiling is the median of the last ten builds plus 10%, so growth shows at a tenth and not at the wall. A run goes red above either line. No deploy is killed for memory.
measures.how_measured: scripts/next-build.mjs prints both after every build (step 1.20). The figure reaches a failing check through scripts/timed.mjs where CI makes the build, or through scripts/await-deploy.mjs after a deploy (step 1.21, by the route the third proposed change names). Measurements under a memory cap go in the table of docs/build-memory.md.

measures.name: What the pre-push rule costs an agent session
measures.today: About 11 to 12 minutes of machine time and about 5 GB of memory before each push: lint about 3 minutes, the type check about 3 (183 s measured), the unit run 5 min 34 s (TC-6). A cloud session starts with no lint cache and no build info, so its first push pays all of it. Nothing records it.
measures.target_a: 5 minutes or less for every push with the whole rule kept, and 5 min 30 s for a session's first, while Vitest's cache is cold: lint 15 s, the type check 60 s from a fresh checkout within 4 GB, the unit run 3 min 30 s. 2 minutes (2 min 30 s for the first) where the owner allows a related test run of 85 to 200 files in place of 1,215.
measures.how_measured: pnpm check, made by steps 1.20 and 2.43, runs the rule's commands through scripts/timed.mjs and prints one line of seconds per step. Timed in a fresh clone and again warm, before and after.

measures.name: Numbers of this area that a failing check holds
measures.today: 0 of 12. Nothing records the seconds of lint, the type check, the unit run, an integration shard, a browser job or a build, the build's peak memory, the time from push to live, the tests that needed a retry or the runner-minutes of a push. Nothing counts how often a commit is checked, and nothing pins the tests' configuration. One test pins CI's configuration at all: the Playwright image tags and the list of browser jobs (src/lib/ci-playwright.scan.test.ts, read here).
measures.target_a: 12 of 12. Counts and configuration are exact. Seconds have a ceiling at most 25% above the median of the last ten runs, the build's memory 10%. A weekly check goes red when a ceiling is looser than that, and a check fails when a CI step runs outside the recorder.
measures.how_measured: Count the labels in scripts/ci-budgets.json and the cases in src/lib/ci-once.scan.test.ts. Steps 0.38, 1.20 and 1.21 make ten of the twelve; the tests' configuration, runner-minutes and the weekly check are the first proposed addition.

bar_in_a_sentence: One push lints, checks and type-checks a commit once and builds it twice in CI; the gate before a deploy takes 90 seconds, a job a release waits for 8 minutes, the unit run 3 and a half, and a session's checks before a push 5. The production build keeps a quarter of its machine free, and a failing check holds every one of these numbers.
can_the_steps_reach_a: Not as written: they end at a B. Five additions and one yes from the owner make it an A after the last phase. The sums. Checks per push: type checks 5 to 2 (step 0.38) to 1 (3.18); lints 2 to 1 (3.18); schema checks 3 to 1 (0.38); builds in CI 3 to 2 (3.18); test-only deploys 8% to 0 (3.18). Reaches, in phase 3. Gate: 311 s today. With each part at its line it is 15 s of lint (0.38), 60 s of type check (2.42) and about 8 s of tests without the 5.9 s test database (0.39): about 83 s. Reaches 90 s only if the native compiler passes its trial, and step 2.42's own done-when stops at 120 s. Unit run: 807 CPU-seconds by the samples (934 x 0.48, 214 x 0.74, 67 x 3.0). Step 0.39 takes 318 away (934 files at 0.14 s): 490, which is 3 min 23 s by the same ratio. Reaches with 7 s to spare. Step 2.44's component trial is worth 61 more: about 2 min 57 s. Migration release: nothing is recorded, so the distance is an estimate from the workflow's 'about 10 minutes'. Browser jobs lose their 3-minute type check: about 7. Shards lose 72 s each (215 s over three, steps 0.4 and 0.39): about 8 min 48 s. Step 3.18 then puts 573 and 208 browser tests in one job behind one build: about 11 minutes. Stops short by 1 to 3 minutes, and no step shortens a job. Build memory: 90% of 8 GB today. On 16 GB this review's build is at 46%. Reaches with the owner's yes to step 1.21 and not without; nothing holds growth below 75%. Pre-push: 11.6 minutes, less 2.75 (lint, 0.38), less 2.2 (unit run, 0.39), less 2.05 (type check, 2.42): about 4.6. Reaches for later pushes. A session's first stays near 7.5 with a cold lint, and near 9.5 if step 2.42 ends on kept build info, which a new session does not have. Held: 0 of 12 today, 1 after step 0.38, 10 after steps 1.20 and 1.21. The tests' configuration and runner-minutes have no step, and three of phase 0's gains sit inside the 25% band.

shortfalls.what: Step 1.20 holds seconds with ceilings 25% above a median. Three gains of phase 0 are smaller than that band and can come back unseen: the schema imported again by the database client costs 28 s a shard (6%), Drizzle no longer pre-bundled 44 s a shard (9%), the test database built again for the gate's six files 5.9 s of 90 (7%). A setup file added to the unit project at 0.05 s a file is 10% of the run. The bar's per-file figures (0.15 s, 0.10 s, setup under 10%) are samples timed by hand. Step 0.39 splits the tests into three projects by folder, and nothing checks that every file still runs. A cold lint after a lockfile change (about 3 minutes) breaks a 19 s ceiling and teaches people to raise it. Nothing lowers a ceiling when its median falls.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Hold the causes, not only the seconds (add to step 1.20)
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Phase 1, S, with step 1.20. (1) src/lib/ci-once.scan.test.ts also reads vitest.config.mts, vitest.integration.config.mts and package.json. It holds: no setup file or global setup at the root; src/test/admin-english.ts only in the components project; isolate off in the unit project; every src/**/*.test.ts in exactly one project; drizzle-orm pre-bundled in both configs; --cache in the lint script and a cache step in both lint jobs; no schema import in src/db/client.ts. (2) scripts/timed.mjs reads Vitest's duration line: it fails when setup passes 10% of the unit run, and when the files run differ from the files on disk. (3) It labels lint and the type check warm or cold by whether their cache was restored, with a ceiling for each. (4) It prints pnpm install's seconds per job and the push's runner-minutes, with a ceiling on the sum. (5) A weekly workflow reads the last ten runs on main from GitHub's jobs API and goes red when a ceiling in scripts/ci-budgets.json is more than 25% above its median (10% for the build's memory).
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: Five planted cases each turn the unit test or a run red and name the cause: admin-english.ts added to the root's setup files; the optimizer block taken out of the integration config; a test file moved where no project includes it; --cache taken off the lint script; a ceiling raised to twice its median. Every run's summary shows the setup share, files run against files on disk, install seconds and runner-minutes.

shortfalls.what: The bar asks 8 minutes or less for the slowest job a migration release waits for. Step 1.20 records the jobs and writes a ceiling; no step makes a job shorter when it is over. The steward's own item said 'if it is not, the job is split', and that line was lost when the gap was folded into step 1.20. From the workflow's 'about 10 minutes', a shard lands near 8 min 48 s after steps 0.4 and 0.39. Step 3.18 then puts both browser suites in one job behind one build: about 11 minutes by the same arithmetic, and its done-when counts builds and says nothing of time. One push in four carries a migration and waits for these jobs.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Bring every job a release waits for under 8 minutes, and keep it there when the browser suites share a build
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Phase 2, M, once step 1.20 has ten runs. Integration: run a shard's files side by side, each Vitest worker on a database of its own made by scripts/db-template.mjs clone (about a second each), in place of one file at a time on one database. Then try 2 shards in place of 3, which saves an install and a seed per push. Browser suites: set Playwright's workers to the runner's cores. When step 3.18 shares the build and one job would pass 8 minutes, keep two test jobs and hand them the one build as an artifact (the server output without source maps and without the build cache). Not a third build and not a fourth shard.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: Over ten runs on main the median of every job in release's needs is 8 minutes or less in the recorder, each one's ceiling in scripts/ci-budgets.json is 10 minutes or less, src/lib/ci-once.scan.test.ts still holds 2 builds and at most 3 shards a suite, and step 3.18's done-when carries the same 8-minute line.

shortfalls.what: Step 1.21's only line is 75% of the machine. On 16 GB today's build sits near 46%, so it can grow by more than half before anything goes red, and it used up its 0.8 GB of room in the two weeks to 11 November. The step turns the build cache and the extra workers back on without a measurement: by October's figures in docs/build-memory.md that is 7.2 GB of compile and up to 1.9 GB for each of three workers, 81% of 16 GB. It does not say how a figure in Vercel's build log reaches a CI run. And the owner is asked to pay before the two source-map switches, which cost nothing, have been measured under the cap (step 1.20 names only the page worker's).
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Step 1.21, tightened: hold the build's memory within 10% of its median, and measure before paying or switching anything back on
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: (1) First, in step 1.20: measure both switches under an 8 GB cap, enablePrerenderSourceMaps off and turbopackSourceMaps off, and put the rows in docs/build-memory.md. If the peak is 6.0 GB or less the purchase can wait, and the ratchet will say when it cannot. (2) The ceiling in scripts/ci-budgets.json is the median of the last ten production builds plus 10%, never above 75% of the machine. It is raised only with a decision row that names what grew. (3) On a larger machine the build cache, the second and third worker and the type check each come back only if the peak under a 16 GB cap stays at 75% or less. (4) The build's figure reaches CI: scripts/next-build.mjs writes seconds and peak to a small file the site serves, or scripts/await-deploy.mjs reads Vercel's build log with the token that code review step 0.2 also needs. await-deploy prints it in the run's summary and fails the run, not the deploy, above the ceiling.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: docs/build-memory.md holds capped rows for both source-map switches and for each setting turned back on. Ten production builds in a row peak at 75% of their machine or less. A trial build 12% above the median turns its run red though it is under 75%. Every run's summary shows the production build's seconds and peak.

shortfalls.what: Steps 1.20 and 2.43 hold the pre-push rule at 5 minutes 'for a push after a session's first'. A cloud session starts in a fresh container with no lint cache and no build info, and many sessions push once. Its first push pays a cold lint (about 3 minutes), and a cold type check too (about 3 minutes) if step 2.42 ends on kept build info and not on the native compiler: 7.5 to 9.5 minutes against a bar of 5. Step 2.42's done-when names the gate in CI only.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Make the pre-push bar hold for a session's first push (add to steps 2.42 and 2.43)
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: S. pnpm check lints the files changed against origin/main when no lint cache exists, and the whole tree when eslint.config.mjs or pnpm-lock.yaml changed. Lint has no rule that reads a second file, which is why its cache is safe, so the answer is the same; CI's gate still lints the tree. Step 2.42's done-when adds the type check from a fresh checkout: 60 s or less with no build info on a machine where it takes 183 s today. If only kept build info reaches 60 s, the step is done for CI and not for sessions, and this measure stays a B.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: In a fresh clone with dependencies installed and no caches, pnpm check after a one-line change in src/lib takes 5 min 30 s or less (2 min 30 s with the related run), printed by the recorder, and a second run takes 5 minutes or less.

shortfalls.what: Five done-whens say less than the bar, and one small step sits two phases late. 0.38 proves the lint cache on a second local run only, not in the gate, and no longer asks that the three builds' logs show no type check. 0.39 dropped the steward's check that the same 1,215 files and the same number of tests run after the split. 2.42 passes the gate at 120 s, makes a second tsconfig before it has tried the compiler that may make it needless, and inherits a plan to let Vercel's build check again. 3.18 has no line for time. 1.20's done-when leaves out that a step outside the recorder fails. And the skip of a deploy for a test-only push (TC-14, S, the same file as step 0.38) waits in phase 3, while each such deploy is one more build at 90% of its machine.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Steps 0.38, 0.39, 1.20, 2.42 and 3.18: done-whens brought up to the bar, and the test-only skip moved to step 0.38
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: No new work, stronger proofs. 0.38: add that the gate's lint step takes under 30 s on a CI run that restored its cache and that no browser job's build log has a 'Running TypeScript' line; move the test-only deploy skip here from step 3.18. 0.39: add that Vitest's 'Test Files' and 'Tests' totals equal the run before. 1.20: add that a CI step run outside the recorder fails a check, and that pnpm check prints the same seconds in a session. 2.42: the gate's three steps at 90 s; try the native compiler first and make tsconfig.app.json only if the whole program stays over 60 s; drop the second check in Vercel's build. 3.18: add the 8-minute line, and one lint per push beside one type check.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: Each of the five steps' done-whens carries its added line, and a push that changes one *.test.ts file shows pending green with the deploy step skipped at the end of phase 0.

tolerated: The hosts job keeps a build of its own in CI. With the store domain set, every /s/ address redirects to the store's host, so the main suite cannot run on that build. About 80 s of build, one install and one seed per push.
Production is built once more, apart from CI's test builds: it reads production's database and settings, so a test build can never be the deployed one.
While the whole program takes over 60 s to check, the gate checks the app without tests and the static job checks everything: two checks, one of them partial.
One install of 922 MB per runner: 7 a push once the browser suites share a job, 8 today.
A single run may be up to 25% over the median before it goes red, 10% for the build's memory. CI machines vary; the weekly check keeps the ceilings near the median.
A cold lint, about 3 minutes, on the first run after the lockfile or the lint configuration changes. It is recorded under its own label.
Component and database test files keep a fresh worker each if step 2.44's trials show they need one: 281 files, about 360 of the unit run's 490 CPU-seconds.
CI's unit run and a session's first run start with an empty transform cache: about 20 s (estimate).
Every push to main runs every check, also when a newer commit is already there. A run on main is never cancelled, because it may be applying a migration.
Until step 4.3: 67 private tree walkers and the same mocks written out in hundreds of test files. About 15 CPU-seconds a unit run and 2,600 to 3,400 repeated lines.
If the owner says no to step 3.19: one deploy per push, also in a burst.
owner_choices: Step 1.21: pay for Vercel's 16 GB build machine, or build in CI and deploy the prebuilt output? The build runs at 90% of its 8 GB machine and was killed once on 11 November. On 16 GB it sits near 46%, and the build cache and extra workers can come back, which makes each deploy faster; it is paid per build minute, at about 35 builds a day now. The prebuilt route needs no new machine and makes the deployed build the one CI made, but it puts production's settings and database address into GitHub. Turning source maps off in the build is free and is measured first; it may put this choice off by some weeks, not remove it. Without one of the two this area stops at a B.

Step 2.43: what must run before a push? A: everything, as today: about 5 minutes after these fixes, 11 to 12 now. B: lint, the type check and the tests the change can reach, about 2 minutes, with the whole unit suite moved into the deploy gate. Nothing then deploys with a failing unit test, but the gate goes from 90 s back to about 5 minutes, where it is today. C: as B before the push with the gate unchanged; a failing unit test outside the six money files can be live until someone reads the red run. A fourth way, which the panel suggests: the gate runs the same related tests as the session, 85 to 200 files, and the whole suite reports beside the deploy. The gate is then about 2.5 minutes.

Step 3.19: once stores are open, may a CI run skip its deploy when a newer commit is already on main, so a burst of pushes shares one deploy? Each deploy is a whole production build and empties every store's cached pages; there were up to 52 on 11 November. A yes also closes a gap: today the deploy hook builds the head of main, so a second push can go live on the first push's gate before its own gate has finished (ci.yml:306-309). It changes D5's 'at once' by a few minutes.
